source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Tune Up, p.6-4

procedures.title: Breaker point distributor: service
steps: Points with an even gray color and only light roughness or pitting can stay in service.

Clean dirty points with a few strokes of a clean, fine-cut point file; keep the file clean and use it on nothing else. Do not use emery cloth or sandpaper, and only remove scale or dirt rather than dressing the faces smooth.
Clean the cam lobe with solvent, lubricate it with Delco Remy Cam and Ball Bearing Lubricant or equivalent, and turn the cam lubricator wick 1/2 turn.
Replace burned or badly pitted points.
Check point alignment (see figure 5 in the manual), then set the gap with the rubbing block on the high point of the cam lobe.

Check point spring tension with a spring gauge hooked on the breaker lever at the contact, pulling at 90 degrees to the lever; read it just as the points open (points closed, follower between lobes). Replace if out of limits.
Refit the rotor and cap and press all wires firmly into the cap towers.
notes: If points burn or pit early, find and fix the cause in the ignition system or engine (Section 6Y), or new points will fail the same way.
Clean used points with a point file before gauging them with a feeler gauge.
Too much spring tension wears points, cam and rubbing block; too little lets the points bounce, causing arcing, burning and a high-speed miss.
